messages.text: Itauma unlikely to receive Hrgovic rematch

metadata.summary: Moses Itauma is unlikely to receive an immediate rematch with Filip Hrgovic after his world heavyweight title defeat.
metadata.content: Moses Itauma unlikely to receive Filip Hrgovic rematch after shock heavyweight stoppage defeat | Boxing News | Sky Sports Skip to content Moses Itauma unlikely to receive Filip Hrgovic rematch after shock heavyweight stoppage defeat Moses Itauma suffered a surprise ninth-round stoppage defeat to Filip Hrgovic at The O2 in London; 21-year-old British contender faces being unable to secure an immediate rematch Sunday 30 August 2026 14:02, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the IBF heavyweight world title fight between Moses Itauma and Filip Hrgovic. Video credit: Courtesy of DAZN Moses Itauma is unlikely to receive an immediate rematch with Filip Hrgovic after his world heavyweight title defeat. The 21-year-old British contender inflicted a second round knockdown on Hrgovic, but then tired dramatically before being stopped in the ninth round at The O2 in London on Saturday night. Itauma could now be forced to wait for another world title fight as no 1 contender Frank Sanchez is mandatory challenger for the IBF title after initially agreeing a deal to allow Itauma vs Hrgovic to go ahead first. metadata.content: Iliman Ndiaye and Richarlison transfer news: Tottenham and Everton in advanced talks over separate deals | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Transfer Iliman Ndiaye and Richarlison transfer news: Tottenham and Everton in advanced talks over separate deals Tottenham discussing potential £60m deal for Everton's Ndiaye - and possible £35m return to Goodison Park for Richarlison; Spurs turn to Ndiaye with previous target Cody Gakpo in talks over Man City move By Lyall Thomas, Vinny O'Connor and Michael Bridge Sunday 30 August 2026 13:25, UK Tottenham and Everton are in advanced talks over transfers for Iliman Ndiaye and Richarlison. A potential fee of £60m for Ndiaye - who has rejected multiple new contract offers from Everton - is being discussed, with conversations over personal terms around a switch to north London also ongoing. Ndiaye, who has scored 17 goals in 74 appearances since joining Everton from Marseille two seasons ago, has also been of interest to Manchester City, but Cody Gakpo - whom Spurs had also targeted - now looks most likely to move to the Etihad . Image: Iliman Ndiaye has also been on Man City's target list for a new forward Everton want to re-sign Spurs striker Richarlison, with a fee of £35m being discussed. messages.text: Hrgovic: Itauma is 'amazing' but boxed like an 'amateur'

metadata.summary: Filip Hrgovic praised Moses Itauma after his shock ninth-round stoppage but said his opponent had boxed “like an amateur”.
metadata.content: Filip Hrgovic: Moses Itauma 'amazing' but boxed 'like an amateur' in thrilling heavyweight fight at The O2 | Boxing News | Sky Sports Skip to content Filip Hrgovic: Moses Itauma 'amazing' but boxed 'like an amateur' in thrilling heavyweight fight at The O2 Filip Hrgovic secured one of the biggest shocks in boxing this year after stopping an exhausted Moses Itauma in the ninth round at The O2; Hrgovic becomes Croatia's first-ever world heavyweight champion By David Rivers Sunday 30 August 2026 11:02, UK Image: Filip Hrgovic lands a punch on Moses Itauma (left) during his win Filip Hrgovic praised Moses Itauma after his shock ninth-round stoppage but said his opponent had boxed “like an amateur”. Hrgovic, 34, became Croatia's first world heavyweight champion at The O2 on Saturday night to win the vacant IBF heavyweight title. Itauma, 21, who was unbeaten coming into the bout, was dominant in the first six rounds after landing a string of accurate blows. But he became visibly exhausted as the fight progressed and he failed to find a way past Hrgovic's durable chin, with the seventh round being the first time in his career he had been past six rounds. metadata.summary: The US Open, of all the four slams, is notoriously the hardest to predict the winners of as it falls at a time of year when eight months into the season the players are more likely than not nursing aches and pains with their bodies battered from the grind of the tour.

It's also played on a surface where more players fancy their chances; many have love-hate relationships with clay and grass but hard courts are their bread and butter.
